title: Kitchen Line Swing
style: 1950s big band swing with upbeat shuffle groove, walking bass, brushed snare, punchy brass hits, and danceable four-bar turns; verse rides tight swing phrasing, pre-chorus strips to rhythm guitar and bass, chorus opens with full horn stabs and handclaps. Female lead vocal with bright belted doubles, playful ad-lib fills, and short call-and-response backing vocals. Trumpet risers, sax falls, and a drum pickup into each chorus. Glossy, lively, vintage stage mix with a big room bounce., big band, pop, female vocals
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You send it back hard
Now I’m on my heels
I keep my eyes low
And I trust what it feels

[Verse 2]
A soft little drop
When you’re pushed way back
That’s a trouble shot
Gives them room to attack

[Pre-Chorus]
But if I drive it deep
Then I make ’em lean
I’m already moving
To the kitchen green

[Chorus]
Drive it deep, drive it deep
(Drive it deep)
Make ’em reach, make ’em leap
(Drive it deep)
If it pops, I’m there
Right on time, right there
Drive it deep, drive it deep
Then I own the net

[Verse 3]
I follow my swing
Then I charge the line
By the time I arrive
That next ball is mine

[Verse 4]
One mistake, one drop
And they taste that win
Now they’re set at the kitchen
Where the points begin

[Pre-Chorus]
But if I drive it deep
Then I take away
All the easy angles
They were hoping to play

[Chorus]
Drive it deep, drive it deep
(Drive it deep)
Make ’em reach, make ’em leap
(Drive it deep)
If it pops, I’m there
Right on time, right there
Drive it deep, drive it deep
Then I own the net

[Bridge]
Don’t gift them a chance
Don’t hand them the line
Make them hit up high
While I close on time

[Final Chorus]
Drive it deep, drive it deep
(Drive it deep)
Make ’em reach, make ’em leap
(Drive it deep)
If it pops, I’m there
Right on time, right there
Drive it deep, drive it deep
Then I own the net
